Everyone Can Now Update to Android Auto 18.2: Here's How To Do It
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
Google has just pressed the go-ahead button for another Android Auto update, bringing the app to version 18.2 in the production channel. Android Auto 18.2 first appeared online approximately one week ago, when Google started the testing phase in the beta program.
The new version isn’t available for all users today through the Google Play Store, as Google continues to use its wave-based rollout system for devices configured to receive app updates automatically. This approach gives the search firm more time to spot bugs in the early stages, preventing a potentially botched update from reaching more devices.
Android Auto 18.2 should appear on the first Android devices as an automatic update as we speak, while everyone else has two options: wait for the new version to show up on the Play Store - which can take up to several weeks - or install the update manually.
Considering the wait can be longer than many people are willing to accept, especially when battling major bugs, the manual update is pretty much the most convenient option.
Here’s how to install Android Auto 18.2 on your device without waiting.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The manual installation of Android Auto 18.2 It all starts with the APK file that you must download from this page . The APK installer allows you to install a certain version of Android Auto on your Android device without using the Google Play Store app distribution engine.
Once you download the file on your device, you must tap it to initiate the update. Make sure you enable permissions for app installations from non-Google Play Store sources. Otherwise, the update will be blocked because the APK file comes from outside the Play Store.
If all permissions are given, the update should complete in just a few seconds. You won’t even need to remove the existing Android Auto version from your device.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Big features coming to Android Auto While Google no longer publishes changelogs for new Android Auto builds, version 18.2 should be good news from a bug-fixing perspective. There are no new front-facing changes, which means the company has been focusing mostly on refining the performance of the app and ironing out the bugs that have been haunting users in the last few weeks.
For example, one of the most recent and widespread glitches blocks notifications on Android Auto . Google has already started an investigation, without actually promising an ETA as to when the fixes could land.
Another bug plagued the experience with Gemini, the AI-powered assistant that has been giving some very frustrating headaches to Android Auto users since the demise of Google Assistant.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Meanwhile, more ambitious updates are already on the horizon. Google plans to bring video app support to Android Auto as part of an update that was announced in the spring of this year. This pretty much means that users will be able to watch videos on their infotainment screens, a feature that would come in handy particularly when waiting to charge the battery.
YouTube will spearhead the foray of video apps into the Android Auto world and will come with an obvious limitation: video playback will be allowed only when your car is parked, as otherwise, it can become a major source of distraction while in motion.
On the other hand, Google is planning to offer uninterrupted playback through video apps on Android Auto, so if you begin driving while watching a video, these applications can automatically switch to an audio-only mode.
This means you’ll be able to listen to the audio track while driving, so instead of looking at the screen, you can focus on the road and still enjoy the content playing in the background. This will come in handy for podcasts or longer videos, where keeping your eyes on the screen isn’t necessarily required.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Additionally, this major Android Auto makeover will also include other new features, such as support for widgets. Users will be able to enable widgets for their favorite apps, such as the calendar and the weather app. These widgets will be shown side by side with the rest of the app, right alongside the navigation card and the rest of the apps on the Coolwalk screen, such as a music player.
Google hasn’t shared an ETA as to when all these features could go live, but their existence has already been observed in beta builds, which is typically a sign that Google is making good progress and is already paving the way for their introduction in production versions. It was originally expected to get these features by the end of this year, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see this happening for users enrolled in the beta program.
The production channel is more likely to receive the big updates in the first quarter of 2027, but everything can change overnight, considering Google has so far remained tight-lipped on pretty much all details.

Made for a Real-Life James Bond: Skyfall Mansion Is a Fanboy's Wildest $3 Million Dream
25 photos
Photo: Fine&Country
As James Bond is getting ready to enter into a new, Amazon-owned era with actor Robert Pattinson, now's as good a time as ever to check out what must be the wildest, most insane James Bond tribute-mansion ever. It's called Skyfall and it's back on the market for the second time in as many years.
Skyfall, the mansion, is often described in the British media as an architectural masterpiece, a theatrical piece of real estate that blends the luxuries of modern life with the most exquisite materials and artwork, James Bond movie references and actual film memorabilia collected over the years. It is theatrical alright, and will do a similarly passionate 007 fan – and multi-millionaire – proud.
As luck would have it, Skyfall is for sale again, one year after being listed publicly and with a considerable price cut. Times are rough for multi-millionaires as well, and the owner of this mansion, a self-professed James Bond fan that's often referenced in the media as a "Daniel Craig lookalike," is even willing to part with the mansion with many of the items shown in photos and the video below.
That doesn't include his personal car collection , three cars from which are shown in the tour in the detached, climate-controlled three-car garage on the property. Dean Reep, the owner of the mansion, has spent about as much money and time to put together an auto gallery worthy of a real-life James Bond.
Photo: Fine&Country It includes, besides Ferraris, Land Rovers, and one ghost-white Countach, a 007 Land Rover with the N007 license plate and one Aston Martin DBS with another 007-inspired plate.
The mansion, located in Nottinghamshire some distance from London, sits on a property Reep bought in 2017 and then proceeded to turn into his dream family home, which also happens to be the wildest James Bond tribute . It was first listed one year ago and is back on the market now, but it is still not complete. It can also be further modified to increase the number of bedrooms.
As it is now, Skyfall features two formal reception rooms, a chef's kitchen with premium appliances and custom cabinetry, a games room, a separate gym with a detached bedroom, six bedrooms with ensuite bathrooms, two separate greenhouses, and a bar with another games room with a wraparound gallery that doubles as a James Bond museum.
Photo: Fine&Country The listing mentions that the gallery can be turned into three more bedrooms, should the next owner wish to have a higher occupancy.
Another highlight is the garage and the spacious motorcourt, with the former offering extra space on top that can be turned into a staff annex or separate accommodation for extended family . A large outdoor lounge space, a pavilion, and a Wimbledon-like tennis court are also available, with perfectly manicured gardens offering privacy and gorgeous spaces for walking.
The listing also describes Skyfall as "grandiose," which is definitely accurate. The styling is not subtle, despite what the same listing will have you believe, as neither are the film references.
Photo: Fine&Country But there is beauty behind this agglomeration of artifacts and memorabilia, from the gorgeous carved staircase to the stained glass windows, the silk tapestry on the walls, or the elaborate carvings integrated even in the most surprising spaces, like the ground-floor bathroom.
Speaking of that bathroom, it also comes with a secret door that leads down to a 3,000 square-foot (279 square-meter) cellar.
The master suite offers, in addition to a massive walk-in his and hers wardrobe two people could easily call home and an ensuite spa bathroom, an actual leather chair used during production of the film Spectre and stunt jackets from Quantum of Solace and Skyfall .
Photo: Fine&Country Normally, collectibles as valuables as these would not be included with the sale of the house they're in, but the owner says he's willing to part with them. Also part of the sale are Sir Roger Moore's gold-plated Seiko Moonraker watch, Rare Aston Martin DB5 blueprints, original Aston Martin Lagonda factory memorabilia, more film set items from Skyfall and Quantum of Solace , and signed memorabilia from Bond actors.
Up in the gallery that overlooks the antique snooker table in the bar is a home office where the owner installed an Aston Martin seat from one of the vehicles Jeremy Clarkson used on Top Gear. From what you can see in the video tour, the owner and his wife are not just James Bond fans, but passionate cinephiles and passionate collectors of car-related memorabilia, so this pick should not come as a surprise.
Highlights of the mansion include a pair of stag statues that overlook the electric gates and are a tribute to the home in the film Skyfall , giant portraits from the James Bond universe on the walls, rare fabrics and materials used in the most creative ways, beautiful artwork, and 11,000 square feet (1,022 square meters) in total of living space, spread between the main house and the annex.
Photo: Fine&Country When Skyfall was first listed, it was asking £3 million (€3.6 million or $4 million at the current exchange rate). That asking price has now been reduced to £2.25 million (€2.7 million or $3 million).

Hyundai Takes Over the Starion Name From Mitsubishi For a Tiburon Reborn Across Imagination Land
10 photos
Photo: Theottle / YouTube
Apparently, some folks believe – or at least secretly hope – that compact and more affordable front-wheel drive coupe models are making a comeback. There are some fresh hints, indeed, but it remains to be seen if it’s just a momentary whim or not.
As prices go up across the world and the US has reached a new average new vehicle transaction price soaring above $51k, the automakers are finally beginning to understand that they also need to address the bottom line. They don’t want to, not really since fat profits is their ultimate goal, but found a way to disguise some of their greed.
For example, there’s a potential revival of the slightly more affordable compact front-wheel drive coupe segment. Honda has already brought back the Prelude and made it a cool Type R-related hybrid model to excuse their not-so-affordable pricing in places like the United States.
Toyota is also rumored to bring back the beloved Celica nameplate, and it should come back to life with FWD and eventually with AWD to honor its rallying legacy. Also, at the 2026 Paris Motor Show in France, the good folks over at Peugeot have hinted, among other things, that they might consider bringing back the fancy RCZ coupe .
Well, someone now asks – “What about the Koreans?” He’s not a nobody, either, but rather a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, this virtual artist, better known as " Theottle " on social media, has resorted to CGI slicing and dicing another coupe to prove his love of sports cars.
So, after his previous attempt – a quirky Subaru SVX grand tourer that came back to life sporting the “signature window-within-a-window glass design” but also a thoroughly modern design, here’s the pixel master saying that since models like Kia's Forte Koup disappeared nearly a decade ago, and Hyundai discontinued the Avante/Elantra Coupe back in 2014, there’s not much to talk about their presence in the space.
He intends to alleviate that omission in his latest behind-the-scenes making-of video , as that got him thinking: “What if Hyundai reintroduced a coupe as a sporty companion to the Avante (Elantra), or perhaps as a spiritual successor to the underrated Tiburon, which ended production in 2008?”
With that goal in mind, the CGI expert created this unofficial, hypothetical design project based on the eighth-generation Hyundai Avante, which is most likely coming as the latest iteration of the Elantra to North America to celebrate its worldwide debut at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show at the end of November (20-29).
“Taking things a step further, I imagined a reborn Tiburon adopting a rear-wheel-drive layout (thus the Infiniti Q60 base), setting it apart from the new Prelude and Celica while giving it a chance to compete with cars like the Nissan Z and Toyota GR86,” explains the author, his line of thought.
However, there’s a new name – Hyundai Starion, and the virtual artist doesn’t forget to explain that one either: “As the rendering evolved, I noticed something unexpected. The sleek proportions and distinctive profile began to resemble the iconic Mitsubishi Starion of the 1980s. So, without apology, I decided to give this concept a fitting name: The Hyundai Starion.”
So, what do you think – yay or nay? Should Hyundai consider bringing back the Tiburon with a potential new name or not?

The Blue Oval company has recently showcased the Ford Expedition Tremor: Project Overland as a bespoke off-road-focused family adventure SUV. As such, are we surprised that the rumor mill is thinking more extensively about the fifth generation of the full-size SUV?
The model, which has been around since the 1997 model year, competing with models like the Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban or GMC Yukon and Yukon XL along with others like the Toyota Sequoia, Nissan Armada, and the Jeep (Grand) Wagoneer, came to life with its fifth iteration approximately two years ago, in October 2024.

The host believes the massive family-oriented SUV will receive both a front-end redesign with a new lighting signature and ample changes to the bumpers and grille, as well as some interior changes.

Man Sells Rare Pontiac Can Am With the Perfect Package: Survivor, Original, Unrestored
30 photos
Photo: eBay seller old56frontier
The Can Am. What a car. This 1977 specimen is here with a package that you don’t find too often. Unrestored, all original, and still with the factory engine under the hood. Sure, it’s not as old as a 1958 Impala or a 1964 1/2 Mustang, but it’s still a Pontiac that still sports all the goodies that you found on the car when you picked it up from the dealer.
The owner doesn’t share many specifics on the car’s past, but this Pontiac somehow survived the test of time with flying colors. It does require some occasional touches, but considering it’s an unrestored car, the simple fact that the original engine starts and runs is still impressive.
The vehicle is now looking for a new home, and I wouldn’t be surprised to learn that it ends up in a museum. You don’t find a Can Am in this shape very often, that’s for sure.
Photo: eBay seller old56frontier Launched in 1977 as a LeMans Sport Coupe package, the Can Am debuted with a tagline that pointed to the Trans Am. “Created in the Trans Am tradition,” Pontiac said, clearly trying to take advantage of the growing appetite for the Trans Am in the United States.
The Trans Am was already the best-selling Firebird version in the lineup, so the GM brand had every reason to hope that the Can Am would also sell like hotcakes.
The Can Am could only be had in Cameo White with black-painted rocker moldings, blacked-out grille, body color twin sport mirrors, and body color Rally II wheels. Every Can Am sported a tri-tone colored accent tape strip on the hood, front fenders, doors, and sport mirrors, and this is the easiest way to tell it apart from the rest of the models.
It obviously came with special Can Am tags on the body.
As for power, the Can Am was fitted with a 400 four-barrel V8 engine, except in California, where Pontiac installed a 403 four-barrel. The engine was paired with a Turbo Hydra-matic transmission, and every car got power front disc brakes, front and rear stabilizer bars, and power steering.
If money wasn’t an issue, buyers could also order additional optional features, such as air conditioning, custom color-keyed seat belts, a front-seat console, and a custom sport steering wheel.
Photo: eBay seller old56frontier The first thing I would recommend for people interested in buying this Can Am is a live inspection. Sure, this might be difficult if you don’t live close to the owner’s location, but considering the intriguing claims, such as the car being a survivor, I think this is the most effective way to make sure that everything is as advertised.
The vehicle should have a 400 V8 engine under the hood, and based on the photos, this is the unit currently in charge of putting the wheels in motion. “The engine is quiet and not smoking,” the seller explains. The transmission shifts smoothly, so it’s impressive that everything is working so smoothly, especially without a previous restoration.
The power windows and locks still work, and so does the AM/FM radio. This car is a little piece of automotive history, so I expect it to sell quite fast.
Photo: eBay seller old56frontier As for the repairs that it needs, the quarters suffer from obvious rust issues, and you’ll want to check the driver’s front floor. This one is rusted out, according to the seller, and this is a sign that the Can Am might have been sitting for quite some time in an area where the humidity level wasn’t necessarily perfect.
A walkaround video or a live inspection should help determine the condition of the metal more accurately, so you know what you have to do if you think this Can Am has a place in your garage.
If everything is as advertised, the body should be very straight. It has never been wrecked, the seller says.
Photo: eBay seller old56frontier The selling price isn’t necessarily surprising, with the owner believing that $11,500 is a fair expectation. The price is non-negotiable, as the seller did not enable the Make Offer option on eBay, meaning that this is exactly how much you have to pay to buy the car.
The vehicle is parked in Olathe, Kansas, and considering its shape, you should be able to drive it home on its wheels. This is good news from a cost perspective, as you won’t have to pay the shipping costs to bring this car to your garage.
On the other hand, if you can’t go there in person, maybe a third-party verification would come in handy, especially if you’re interested in buying this car for a collection. The car is a survivor that has never been restored, but there’s no information on any paperwork that might be included in the sale. You’ll get a title, but the build sheet and the owner’s manual might not be available.

Dear Petrolheads, Get Ready for the First-Ever BMW M3 Electric – Rendering
9 photos
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii
BMW is up to no good these days, as while the Neue Klasse design language keeps getting criticized, the company does not care about it. The Neue Klasse models have a face only a mother could love, save for a few exceptions, of course, and their cockpits, which look pretty much the same for what it’s worth, probably won’t age that well.
Thus, if you were dreaming to change your G2X, F3X, or E9X 3er, or perhaps an even older one with the new G50 a few years from now, when the depreciation will hit it like a train on the used car market, then chances are you will probably look for something else. Or would you? Guess only time will tell if the G5X is indeed an upgrade or a downgrade over some of its predecessors.
Mind you, the Neue Klasse design language is definitely here to stay, and it will also be applied to the upcoming BMW M3 . The premium compact sports sedan (and Touring) is gearing up to take an inevitable swing at the Mercedes-AMG C 63 and Audi RS 5, and it is in the making as we speak. It will follow the same recipe, as it will be visually more aggressive than the new-gen 3er, while also featuring a dedicated chassis setup, uprated brakes, a few changes on the inside, and more power than the M350.
The latter is the current range-topping member of the new-gen BMW 3 Series family, and has 437 horsepower to play with. The output equals 443 metric horsepower and 325 kilowatts, as that is how much is 3.0-liter twin-turbo straight six with 48V mild-hybrid assistance develops. The mill produces 428 pound-feet (580 Nm) of torque, and enables 0-60 mph (97 kph) in just 4.1 seconds, and that is the same as the 2027 M3 Sedan (base model), which has 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW).
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii We have yet to find out how punchy the all-new BMW M3 will be, but word on the street is that it might come with over 600 horsepower. The mill of choice will likely be the familiar 3.0-liter straight-six with dual turbos, which should also get mild-hybrid assistance. The upcoming M3 is understood to show its face in an official environment, with no camouflage on its body, sometime in 2028, perhaps touching down in USA for the 2029 model year.
In 2027, the company is expected to launch the first-ever BMW M3 Electric. Yes, you read that right, an all-quiet alternative to the ICE-powered M3 is being developed as we speak. And while it will utilize the iconic M3 moniker, it won’t share its nuts and bolts with its gas-powered sibling, nor with the regular 3 Series models. That’s because it will be the range-topping version of the new i3 Sedan, so it will utilize the same Neue Klasse NAx platform.
The model will feature a dedicated chassis setup, too, as well as beefier brakes to keep the extra oomph in check. Expect a few sporty changes on the inside, as well, and the exterior will be inspired by the M Concept Neue Klasse. The study premiered earlier in 2026, and has so far been used on most renderings trying to decipher what lies beneath the fake skin (camouflage).
The same goes for the model imagined by @avarvarii recently and shared in the gallery, which features familiar front and rear bumper, and a vented front hood, among other things. These were inspired by the show car mentioned above. This rendered BMW M3 Electric definitely looks a lot more aggressive than the new i3 Sedan on which it was based. It’s presented in yellow in this case, has some M logos, and a set of retro-inspired wheels, from what we can tell.
Photo: Instagram | avarvarii Depending on whom you ask, you’d get different answers when it comes to how punchy this model will be. Some believe it might have in the region of 700 (metric) horsepower in total, whereas others would try to convince you that a four-digit (metric) output is possible. We think that some 700 to 800 ps sounds more realistic.
BMW’s first-ever M3 Electric will feature a quad-motor setup with all-wheel drive, and will also have the 800-volt technology for quicker charging times. It will take an inevitable swing at the Mercedes-AMG C-Class, which is believed to have some 800 hp available via the right pedal.
As we already told you, the BMW M3 Electric is expected to launch sometime in 2027, whereas its ICE-powered sibling based on an updated version of the CLAR platform should follow it the next year.
Now, is the zero-emission M3 something that you look forward to? What’s your take on the design as imagined by the quoted artist? Would you ever see yourself driving one of these? BYD is preparing to launch a new flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.
BYD previews new flagship MPV ahead of its debut
We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.
Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the new flagship MPV is coming soon.
“A new creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo said after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously said the company expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.
Although it’s blurred, the preview shows a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.
It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.
The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.
BYD Ocean MPV test car (Source: Autohome)
In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.
While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.
The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD said earlier this year.
BYD Ocean-V MPV concept (Source: BYD)
BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.
The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.
Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.
BYD Xia MPV (Source: Lu Tian)
The Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).
BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.
Zhuo said to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

Dodge Ram Truck Looks Beat Up Until You Pop the Hood
17 photos
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube
You wouldn't give a dime for this 1994 Dodge Ram 1500. It is a beat-up, run-down, moss-covered truck that was left to rot for a few years before it was rescued. However, a diesel mechanic paid $6,000 to take it home and says it might have been worth much more.
Luckily, the massive downpour in which TJ Lamb from Magnacars films alongside David, the new owner of the truck, might wash away years of neglect. David is a diesel mechanic who also builds turbos and one who can’t stand to see a car left to rot. He bought this 1994 Dodge Ram 1500 from someone who no longer needed it. But he did, and had big plans with it.
The Dodge Ram had been a burnout truck before it was abandoned, and it had already been V10-swapped. The donor engine came from a 1998 Viper GTS that was wrecked by the previous owner at just 30,000 to 40,000 miles (48,280 to 64,374 kilometers) on the clock. So he swapped it into the truck.
" Nobody would believe how much I bought it for, " David says, because he knows he got lucky. He paid $6,000 for the truck. The V10 alone would have been an $8,000 deal without even sitting under the hood of a vehicle. Everything about the engine was fine, but he couldn't say the same about the truck that it came with.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube Abandoned for years, covered in dust and grime, with green moss growing on top of the white paint, partially enveloping the truck in green, it looked like the earth had started to claim it. That is just Pacific Northwest kind of patina. The weather is anything but kind in the area. David is keeping that original patina for the moment, but at some point, he is going to swap this look for an RT/10 concept truck from the 1990s.
Nope, Dodge never built that concept truck, but David will, with inspiration from the 1996 Dodge Ram VTS. “Similar but in my own style.” He will also install 18-inch Viper wheels with grippier tires, Mickey Thompsons on the rear axles, because he will need all the grip he can get when he hits the drag strip. He will also put on bigger brakes because he will need all the braking power he can get.
The new owner has had the truck since February and has been working on it since. There is always something he has to fix. His Dodge Ram is, after all, a 32-year-old truck. When he brought it home, it was an absolute mess. The front suspension was shot, the brakes were useless, the steering didn’t work, and the clutch was blown.
It came with the T56 six-speed manual transmission from the Viper, but it didn’t shift, so he installed a Tremec TR-6060 out of a 2008 fourth-generation Viper. Now, he is running a twin-disc clutch setup, capable of withstanding up to 1,000 horsepower. He is still far behind that. The V10 now makes between 600 and 700 horsepower at the wheel.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube David dropped the truck on Belltech drop spindles up front to make it look more aggressive, as if it didn't already, with its grille-less front end and fans and radiator exposed. Everything is there for a reason, while the truck looks like the ultimate sleeper.
The rear still sits at its standard height, but David plans to drop it four inches. The truck is sitting on a 9-inch rear end, but it has a 3.50 Positraction in it, which is a little too tall for the six-speed, David complains. At 80 mph (129 kph) in the sixth gear on the highway, he is at only 1,200 rpm. So there is plenty of room for more. And he seems determined to get more.
Now, he is daily driving the 32-year-old truck just for the fun of it. He does burnouts in it and plans to drag race it with a new setup. He has taken it to car meets, and he must admit his truck was the shock factor of the event every time. The beat-up Ram makes tons of power, and the Valvetronic 3-inch mufflers roar out all the drama from under the hood.
David will also swap the factory seats for a pair of Viper buckets and a vintage instrument cluster. Right now, he's got wires dangling from the dashboard, but it's getting better. At least the dashboard is not cracked after so many years of neglect. But the windshield is.
Photo: Magnacars | YouTube
How many miles does the truck have on the clock right now? Well, the owner has no idea. The odometer stopped working at 166,000 miles (267,151 kilometers).
David also drives around in a lifted 2015 Volkswagen Golf TDI , looking like a rally car, while working on a 1991 Golf that he TDI-swapped. The next move is to make it all-wheel drive.

The brokerage arm of J.B. Hunt won one and lost one in an Arizona federal court Thursday in what now is shaping up to be one of the key cases on broker liability as the industry moves to a new legal landscape following the decision in Montgomery vs. Caribe Transport II.
The U.S. District Court for Arizona accepted one J.B. Hunt request for summary judgment in the case of Crystal Gee et. al. vs. J.B. Hunt et. al. But it rejected another.
Plaintiff Crystal Gee is the guardian of the children who were injured in the crash and left without their parents in the fatal crash that is the subject of the lawsuit.
The tragedy that led to the lawsuit occurred in October 2023. A truck driven by Shokhijakhon Bekmuradov, an employee driver of carrier Borderlanders Inc., crossed into the lane of oncoming traffic on U.S. Route 160, a two-lane highway. However, according to the recap by Judge Stephen McNamee, Bekmuradov did not immediately return to his normal lane.
A car heading the other way and carrying Gregory Cox, his partner Lindsey Watson, and their three children came around a corner. That car collided headon with Bekmuradov’s truck. Cox and Watson were killed and the three children were seriously injured, according to the recap.
The load was being shipped by medical equipment supplier Lincare which had hired J.B. Hunt’s brokerage arm to move its products. It was going from Denver to Phoenix, according to the recap. (The price of the load: $1,350). Borderlanders booked the load off the J.B. Hunt online broker’s platform.
Two requests for dismissal
J.B. Hunt requested summary judgment in its favor on two grounds. It sought a dismissal on the plaintiffs’ charge that it was vicariously liable for the driver’s actions and that Bekmuradov was a “statutory employee” of J.B. Hunt. It also sought dismissal on the plaintiffs’ charge that J.B. Hunt’s hiring of Borderlanders was negligent.
The carrier/ intermodal /brokerage giant was successful on the first request. But it was not successful on the second request, and the case will go forward.
J.B. Hunt (NASDAQ: JBHT) declined comment on the case, citing the ongoing litigation.
The original defense put up by J.B. Hunt originally relied on the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act (F4A) and its prohibition against state action that might impact a “price, route or service.” In its initial response in the case, which the plaintiffs had first filed in March 2024, J.B. Hunt also said it could not be brought into the action as a broker because the safety exception to F4A, which does allow state action on safety-related incidents if they are “with respect to motor vehicles,” didn’t include brokers.
But that defense died with the ruling in Montgomery , forcing J.B. Hunt to find different approaches.
Where J.B. Hunt failed in its argument, allowing the case to proceed, is Judge McNamee’s ruling that the plaintiffs “have presented sufficient evidence in which a rational jury could find that J.B. Hunt knew, or should have known, of the safety risks associated in selecting Borderlanders to transport the Load.”
The plaintiffs had argued that Borderlanders had a problematic past. In an earlier filing, it said the carrier had a “history of hiring inexperienced and incompetent drivers that put the motoring public at risk of catastrophic injury or death.” They said J.B. Hunt should have known that when it hired Borderlanders.
Borderlanders is not part of the action before the Arizona federal court. According to the judge’s decision, the carrier has settled with the plaintiffs and an action against Bekmuradov was dismissed voluntarily with prejudice, ending the case.
That fact is part of the J.B. Hunt argument against the negligent hiring claim. “J.B. Hunt contends that there remains no underlying tort claim against Borderlanders so Plaintiffs cannot prove an essential element of their negligent hiring claim against J.B. Hunt,” Judge McNamee writes in his summary.
Carrier’s safety record
J.B. Hunt, according to the judge, has said the plaintiffs have not provided evidence that Borderlanders had a checkered past. But the judge didn’t accept that.
“Plaintiffs cite evidence that J.B. Hunt never reviewed Borderlanders’ publicly available accident and crash history, and FMCSA safety scores, safety assessment alerts, and inspection violation history before selecting Borderlanders,” the judge writes.
And he agreed. “There remain factual disputes regarding Plaintiffs’ negligent hiring claim against J.B. Hunt, therefore, the Court denies J.B. Hunt’s Motion on this claim,” Judge McNamee wrote.
What the court accepted
On the J.B. Hunt request for summary judgment that was granted by the court, the company’s argument, according to the judge’s filing, is that it was “not liable under the federal leasing regulations because there was no lease between J.B. Hunt and Borderlanders.”
The court agreed with that view. “In this case, it is undisputed that Borderlanders transported the Load under its own authority using its own equipment and driver,” the judge wrote. “Based on the undisputed material facts, J.B. Hunt did not lease equipment to Borderlanders. Thus, there is no lease, and the federal leasing regulations are inapplicable.”
Those regulations that might have held J.B. Hunt vicariously liable “apply only if there is a valid lease,” according to the decision.
View from an outsider
Gregory Reed, a partner at the law firm of Hanson Bridgett and head of its transportation practice, said in an email to FreightWaves that J.B. Hunt’s arguments were “common refrains in the broker and logistics industry.” But he also described them as “unavailing.”
Reed summed up J.B. Hunt’s arguments.
One, according to Reed, was that “Borderlanders remained a FMCSA-authorized (albeit unrated) carrier thus brokers should be free to use such carriers insulated from negligence.”
That goes to the heart of what numerous industry officials have argued in the wake of Montgomery: brokers lack guidelines on what steps they need to take to protect themselves against negligent hiring claims in a lawsuit.
That was particularly stark in the recent Texas nuclear verdict against C.H. Robinson, where it was hit with a more than $600 million verdict despite the carrier it hired in the 2021 wreck that led to three deaths had a Satisfactory rating from FMCSA.
That question of what constitutes sufficient vetting is not as clear in the J.B. Hunt case, since Borderlanders, according to numerous references in the lawsuit’s various briefs, did not have a stellar safety record.
Reed said the second argument by J.B. Hunt was that “Borderlanders’ safety and performance record was insufficient to provide JB Hunt notice because negative incidents were few compared to the carrier’s number of drivers and volume of loads.”
With enough of J.B. Hunt’s arguments rejected that the case will proceed, a jury may be the next step to take up the issue.
“Both (J.B. Hunt) arguments go to the duty of care a company like JB Hunt is required to exercise based on what it should have known, and their failure at this stage in the case demonstrates that courts may be unlikely to take these cases out of the hands of the jury to determine reasonableness,” Reed said.

23 New Kaido House, Mini GT, Pop Race and Tarmac Works Collectibles for November 2026
54 photos
Photo: Kaido House
Just a few days ago I unboxed 10 Hot Wheels cars that were a real bargain. Some might say they’re genuine peg-warmers, but that perspective might not be valid a few years from now. My next story will include 10 Ferraris from Mattel but I’m planing to do something different during the final days of November.
I will be comparing Hot Wheels collectibles to products from other manufacturers. I thought I was all set to go for that story, as I had already bought a Car Culture 2-Pack for the job.
However, I figured the Kaido House, Mini GT and Ixo models were individually worth as much as the 2-pack, which wasn’t entirely fair. So, I decided to upgrade and give Mattel an equal fighting chance by picking up two Elite 64 items.
I’ve only previously bought the Porsche 993 GT2 from that series, and I can tell you there’s another Porsche on the new list, too.
Now, I’m just giving you a preview of what’s coming this month, and I’d like to focus on some of the newest 1/64th-scale pre-orders on the market next. You could pay as much as $500 for all these, so it might be smarter to just purchase the ones you’re the most excited about.
Kaido House Photo: Kaido House I feel like I have been ignoring Jun Imai’s project for too long. I imagine Kaido House was his opportunity to build the tiny cars he loved the most, on a more premium level than he ever could with Hot Wheels.
The company has been around since 2021, and has released several amazing castings since. The latest pre-order includes four models, which could be ready to ship out by Q2 of 2027. The Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32) was the first of two that I wanted to sign up for.
It’s not just because this is my favorite generation of the GT-R, but also because of the Advan livery. I can only recall seeing three previous variations of it, and neither was remotely as good as this one. The other model I might buy is the fictional Kaido Star sporting that wild bosozoku/kaido racer look.
The moment I laid eyes on it I had an instant flashback of some dioramas and similar cars I saw at the Tokyo Auto Salon back in 2016. I don’t think I’d ever like to build a car like this in the real world, but having a tiny version of it at home is one way to recognize a special part of Japanese car culture.
Photo: Kaido House I just hope it won’t be a slippery slope towards getting an unreasonable number of them next. I believe the Lancia Delta HF Integrale is a brand new casting for Kaido House, and it’s a surprising appearance to say the least.
Mr. Imai hasn’t focused solely on Japanese machines so far, as we’ve seen some American cars in the mix. But Lancia is the last car manufacturer I expected to see from Mini GT’s partner brand.
The removable magnetic hood adds a nice touch to an already iconic design, and the red and white color combo is seriously enticing.
The pink finish on the Chevrolet Camaro immediately reminded me of Ken Block’s Hoonipigasus , although the design’s origins are much older than that. It’s an interesting machine for sure, and the twin-turbo engine is the main attraction here.
Mini GT Photo: Mini GT As far as I can tell, the “official”, final Mini GT preorder for November should go live on either the 23rd or the 24th. The last time we had one I had just realized the diecast manufacturer posts a new one every two weeks.
That hasn’t stopped the team from coming out with some special releases in between, and this time both Peanuts and James Bond fans will be pretty happy about the update.
Let’s start with with the two race spec GT-Rs. Snoopy is on the #23 car, while Woodstock is on the #24 racer.
The blue Nissan GT-R NISMO GT3 gets two card variations, as one was a special item for Mini GT’s Yokohama Pop Up Store.
Photo: Mini GT There’s also a paper bag included in the offer if you buy both cars, while supplies last. It’s not something I will be pursuing, but I imagine many fans of the franchise will want a closer look.
The 007 collection seems to have become an important part of the strategy, and I think there are currently 10 items in the pre-order phase.
Think of the Aston Martin DBS (Casino Royale), the Land Rover Defender 110 Crew Cab (Skyfall) or the Aston Martin V12 Vanquish (Die Another Day) to name a few). Now, for me James Bond began with Pierce Brosnan, so I’m not familiar with any of the movies that preceded him.
Seeing the new Mini GT Tuk Tuk (Octopussy) and AMC Hornet X Hatchback (The Man with the Golden Gun) makes me think I should give Roger Moore a chance soon.
Pop Race Photo: Pop Race Now, I am little late in reporting on two of the models here, as the pre-order session closes on November 23rd. I just hope this story reaches you in due time, but even if it doesn’t it shouldn’t be impossible to get ahold of these next year.
The LB Works Supra A90 is a brand new casting for Pop Race , and it doesn’t really mean anything to me. I guess it’s proof that most of the brand’s clients are quite a bit younger than I am. Otherwise, I’d expect more variations of the old Supra. And I don’t just mean the GT300 model that I enjoyed unboxing in July.
The Touge Maou is one of the most iconic versions of the Honda S2000 ever made, at least if you consumed as much as of Hot Version as I did growing up. The J’s Racing version of the car makes the Pandem S2000 look almost boring by comparison, but I might be biased in saying that. I think Pop Race is slightly late to the party though, as Inno64 must have had a tiny replica of this car for at least a year now.
Come to think of it, neither one of my local dealers advertised the pre-order for this car. It’s either that or I completely forgot about it, which is why I know who I’ll be calling the moment I’m done writing this story. Everyone seems to be jumping onboard the 7-Eleven bandwagon these days, so the Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO should come as no surprise. I’ve had enough of this car already!
Tarmac Works Photo: Tarmac Works If you’ve read my interview with Felix Kwong (the man who created Tarmac Works over a decade ago), you’ll know he has a personal connection to the Macau Grand Prix. That said, it’s no wonder his brand is always onsite for some sort of project or new release.
The Pompompurin-themed Mercedes-AMG GT3 will be available both as a 1/64th and 1/43rd scale collectible at the 73rd edition of the event. The same goes for three more race cars on this list: the #11 Porsche 911 GT3 R driven by Ayhancan Guven, the #22 GT3 R driven by Laurin Heinrich, and also the #79 Mercedes-AMG GT4.
If you’re at the race, you might even find Maro Engel’s Initial D-themed Mercedes in the vending machines! For me, pre-ordering one of the eight models in the official pre-order session is a much more accessible option.
The LB-Works Nissan GT-R R35 type 2 is the latest “Tuner & Street” collectible, and it could trigger some nostalgia for those of us who loved 2 Fast 2 Furious.
Photo: Tarmac Works I confess I had no clue that Jorge Lorenzo competed in the Porsche Carrera Cup, but that’s not a good enough reason for me to buy this car as I’m not fond of the color combo.
It couldn’t have been that long ago that we saw a green variation of the Bentley Continental GT3: the new one is a throwback to the 2019 edition of 24 Hours at Spa.
The BMW M4 GT3 and the Porsche 911 Carrera 4 GTS are the two Minichamps Exclusives in this pre-order, and I plan to skip both of them and the Audi Quattro A2 Gr.B Rally car for something else. The Ferrari F355 Challenge looks great in Silver, which isn’t something I will often say.
Meanwhile, the yellow F40 GTE is simply out of this world. And it’s slightly funny knowing I have a similar Hot Wheels collectible with a special feature coming right up.

It is hard to believe that it has already been over 6 years since DDR5 memory was launched, but now in the fall of 2026 it is already time to start talking about the next generation of server memory.
This past week the JEDEC Solid State Technology Association, the industry consortium responsible for developing the various memory standards (among other specifications) released a preview of the in-development DDR6 memory standard.
The next generation of the group’s mainline SDRAM memory standard, DDR6’s development has been known about for quite some time now. But, outside of the customary bandwidth improvements, it has not been clear what other changes the DDR6 specification may bring with it. Now, following JEDEC’s preview, we have our first official look at what some of the major features of the new specification will be – or at least, are expected to be based on the current development plans.
DDR6 Memory Standard Preview: Smaller DIMMs, Bigger Bandwidth
As always, the key improvement in a new generation of DDR memory is the amount of bandwidth available per DIMM. DDR6, in turn, is planned to be a major overhaul of DDR memory technology in this regard, as it is tackling the matter from both ends.
In regards to per-pin bitrates, the current plan calls for DDR6 to start at 12.8 GT/sec and eventually reach 14.4 GT/sec and higher. Currently, DDR5 tops out at 9.2 GT/sec, so at the top end this would represent an eventual 57% increase in per-pin bandwidth. Meanwhile looking at things on a contextual basis, the original DDR5 specification stopped at 6.4 GT/sec, so if DDR6 were to eventually end up on a similar long-term trajectory, then “beyond” could eventually extend well past 14.4 GT/sec.
Still, a 57% increase is not as much bandwidth as some customers would like to see, so the group is also planning to take the more radical step of changing the bit-width of a DIMM itself. Following nearly three decades of DIMMs being 64-bits wide, going back to the days of single data rate SDRAM, the group is proposing to make DIMMs even wider, moving to a 96-bit wide memory bus.
With 32 more data pins (DQ lines), a DDR6 DIMM would offer 50% more bandwidth at identical clockspeeds to a DDR5 DIMM. Or, combining the two improvements, a full DDR6-14400 DIMM would offer 172.8GB/sec of bandwidth, or 2.35x as much bandwidth as a DDR5-9200 DIMM does today (and more still compared to the DDR5-8000 DIMMs that the latest server platforms actually support).

Max Die Density | 128 Gbit | 64 Gbit | 16 Gbit
Max UDIMM Size (DSDR, 1 die) | ? | 128 GB | 32 GB
Max Data Rate | 14.4 Gbps+ | 9.2 Gbps | 3.2 Gbps
Channels | ? | 2 | 1
Total Width (Non-ECC) | 96-bits (4×24-bit?) | 64-bits (2×32-bit) | 64-bits
Banks (Per Group) | 16? | 8 | 4

Voltage (Vdd) | ? | 1.1v | 1.2v
Vddq | ? | 1.1v | 1.2v
The switch to a wider bus width for an individual DIMM will come with some significant ramifications for the rest of the standard as well, in part because of the changes that need to happen in order to enable those wider DIMMs. Key to this, DDR6 will be employing a pseudo-channel architecture that splits up the individual channels.
Unfortunately, JEDEC’s preview announcement does not clarify if and how this might interact with the sub-channel architecture that DDR5 currently employs, so we do not have enough information to definitively state how this compares to DDR5’s architecture in this regard. But broadly speaking, splitting up DIMMs into multiple channels is how the most recent version of the standard was able to raise bandwidth in light of DRAM core clockspeeds having long grown stagnant, and some kind of similar change has been expected for DDR6 as well.
Regardless, the specification is also doubling the number of memory banks on a DIMM, which by our reckoning should bring it up to 16 banks per group. This is another change that should further help DDR6 deliver data at those higher pin bitrates, as it affords more banks that can be used while the other banks are busy refreshing.
The change to the individual DIMM memory bus width will also bring with it some physical changes to DIMM designs – and more than you might be expecting. JEDEC will be introducing a more compact 74mm wide DIMM for DDR6, which on a relative basis is just a bit wider than a DDR5 SO-DIMM. According to the group, the change is being made to allow for systems with higher memory densities as, while routing small traces is bad enough, 16 channels of DDR5 DIMMs takes up an immense amount of physical space that there is no real work-around for with their 133mm module width.
Bull SC26 Chicago-Bull Sequana XH31600 Intel Diamond Rapids w/16 Channel DDR5
Notably, the group’s announcement does not clarify whether they will keep the current DIMM width, which like the 64-bit memory bus has been with the standard since the earliest days. Though JEDEC is quick to note that they are working on multiple form factors, potentially including RDIMMs, UDIMMs, and even CAMMs – the latter of which was added to DDR5 as a mid-generation feature. In that respect, the denser 73mm form factor may end up as a premium option for RDIMMs, especially as a smaller connector combined with a wider memory bus would require some very small pins on the new compact form factor.
Meanwhile, it is interesting to see that, at present, there is no mention of SO-DIMMs at all. So the small laptop DIMM factor may very well be on its way out in favor of CAMMs (or soldiered memory) for all laptops.
On the other hand, the preview announcement mentions server needs front and center. JEDEC’s members are well-aware of the need for more memory in the data center, and this is something that the group is explicitly looking to tackle. In practice, this would seem to be aiming to deliver on all three major features that data center operators are after: smaller DIMMs, more memory bandwidth per DIMM, and higher capacities overall.
Speaking of which, besides allowing for more DIMMs in a given amount of space, the DDR6 specification will also be tackling the memory capacity matter from the other direction as well. As always, the latest standard is increasing the maximum supported die density, bringing it from 64 Gbit to 128 Gbit. At the same time, the spec will make some unspecified optimizations for die stacking to allow for higher capacity packages overall. At present, die stacked DRAM packages are far from brand new, but 3DS DIMMs are still relatively uncommon overall.
Micron DDR5 RDIMM Close Up
A bit more nebulous, the announcement also notes support for multiple ECC implementations. The current DDR5 standard has a single ECC standard at the DIMM level for transmission and overall DIMM reliability, as well as on-die ECC to protect/correct the individual cells. In the past year we have seen some proposals for layering additional soft ECC on top of this to further improve reliability (e.g. Astera Labs’ Leo CXL memory expanders ), so it may be that JEDEC is eyeing something similar, to let customers allocate additional DRAM capacity to storing ECC data for even higher levels of reliability.
Finally, the DDR6 standard will be taking steps to rein in the power consumption of DIMMs, which has been a concern with every generation as increased performance comes will otherwise drive up the power needs. For the next version of the spec, DDR6 will be switching to VSS-terminated I/O, as opposed to DDR5’s VDDQ-based termination – in effect terminating with a low voltage instead of a high voltage. The spec will also introduce low power modes for data center use, though the initial announcement does not go into further detail. Regardless, the consortium is targeting “significantly improved performance-per-watt” versus DDR5, which would be welcome across the board, but especially in data centers where power is a constraining factor and large DIMM counts are eating up larger amounts of that budget.
Final Words
Wrapping things up, JEDEC’s initial announcement for DDR6 emphasizes how the group has significant plans for the next generation of the memory standard. While it is true that every generation of DDR has been faster and lower power than the previous, how this is accomplished has changed with every generation – and it gets harder all the time. Meanwhile the physical DIMM changes are even more remarkable, and they underscore how the group is ready to break away from the form factors that have defined SDRAM for almost the last 30 years.
The net impact of these changes, in turn, stands to be significant. A 2.35x bandwidth increase on its own is quite remarkable. Accomplishing that while also shrinking the width of a DIMM by 44% is even more so. Consequently, DDR6 as currently proposed stands to be a big change indeed.
As for when we might see a complete specification, or better still physical DIMMs, that will have to wait. This preview was just that: an early look at a specification still under development, and a not-too-subtle reminder to the industry that if they want to see more and participate in the development process, they need to be part of the JEDEC. On which note, the JC-42 workgroup will be meeting in Hawaii at the end of this month for their final quarterly meeting of the year.

Rare 1969 Dodge Charger Daytona Has Been in the Same Family Since New, True Hemi Gem
19 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Introduced in 1966, the Dodge Charger hit NASCAR ovals as soon as it arrived in showrooms. It won the title that very first year, but it struggled during the following season. With the regular Charger unable to keep up with the Ford Torino Talladega , Dodge developed more aerodynamic versions.
In 1969, Dodge created the Charger 500. Compared to the R/T, it featured a 1968 Coronet grille, while the rear window was made flush with the rest of the roof. These changes reduced both drag and lift. However, the 500 still wasn't quick enough for the Torino Talladega on the high-bank oval tracks.
Later that year, Dodge took things up a notch and developed the Daytona. Far more radical than the Charger 500, the Daytona was a whopping 18 inches (457 mm) longer thanks to a nose cone, while massive wing sat 23 inches (547 mm) atop the trunk.
To make the Daytona eligible for NASCAR racing, Dodge was required to sell at least 500 cars to the general public. Mopar eventually put together 503 examples, which sold like hotcakes. At the time of its introduction, the Daytona was by far the most radical production vehicle available in the United States.
The Charger Daytona came standard with the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) RB V8, which was also the base mill in the R/T. The unit delivered 375 horsepower and 480 pound-feet (651 Nm) of torque. The 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi, rated at 425 horsepower and 490 pound-feet (664 Nm), was on the options list.
Most Daytonas rolled off the assembly line with the standard engine. Specifically, 433 units got the 440 V8. The figure is split between 139 cars equipped with the four-speed manual and 294 fitted with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic.
The remaining 70 units were ordered with the 426 Hemi. Exactly 22 customers went with the four-speed manual, while 48 opted for the comfort of the automatic gearbox. The B5 Blue example you see here is one of those Hemi automatic rigs, and it's quite stunning.
Ordered new at Walt Sparrow Dodge in Greeley, Colorado, this Daytona soldiered on for over 50 years with its 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8 still intact. What's more, it's a highly original example with just one repaint in the original color.
In the care of the same family since new, the Mopar has only 43,041 miles on the odometer and an overall condition that makes it suitable as a museum display. It also has the desirable A32 Super Performance Axle Package, which pairs the drivetrain with a Dana 60 Sure Grip rear end with a 4.10 ratio.
This Charger Daytona recently popped up among the lots that will go under the hammer at Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction . It will change hands on January 15, and there's no way that it will fetch less than $700,000. Assuming that bidding will blow past the reserve, this Daytona may become one of the most expensive units ever sold at public auction.
For reference, the most expensive Hemi Daytona sold for $3.3 million in 2024. Two more cars traded for seven-figure sums. One sold for $1.43 million in 2023, while another winger warrior fetched $1.32 million in 2026.

Audi Will Build a New-Generation A8 After All. This Is Why It Might Not Make It to the U.S.
14 photos
Photo: Audi
Audi pulled the plug on the A8 with no successor in sight. However, it turns out that the Ingolstadt-based automaker is, indeed, working on a flagship sedan to replace the D5 generation, just not for America. The German firm is negotiating the use of a Chinese platform, a move that would lock the luxury sedan out of the U.S.
Audi stopped taking orders for the A8 in Germany in February 2026. Production of the sedan ended at the Neckarsulm factory in Germany in mid-October 2026, after a 32-year run . The German automaker never said anything about a successor. Until now.
Now, the automaker brings back hope to those who were planning to buy a new generation of the A8. The all-time rival of the Mercedes-Benz S-Class and BMW 7 Series is making a comeback before 2030. The automaker confirmed to Auto Bild España that a next-generation model will be rolled out with a hybrid powertrain.
However, Audi might have to keep the A8 out of America. And that is because the carmaker is considering using a Chinese platform for the upcoming model. While the model will retain the internal combustion engine, almost certainly running on gas, it will be paired with an electric motor rather than fully transitioning to an EV-only lineup.
Photo: Audi However, in a conversation with Auto Bild España, the automaker's representatives declined to confirm the ongoing rumors concerning a partnership with Huawei for a potential jointly developed architecture. The architecture is built for pure electric or range-extended electric (EREV), tailored to Chinese luxury buyer preferences. In the meantime, both Europe and the U.S. markets still demand hybrids.
A Huawei-developed platform built in China cannot be sold in the U.S. due to connected-vehicle software/hardware bans, issued by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security. The architecture should go into production at the FAW-Audi joint-venture plant in Changchun to utilize spare capacity.
The platform will not be imported to the U.S. and might not comply with European standards, which means that Audi might have to develop a bespoke platform solely for Europe and the U.S., which sounds more like a money pit than a profitable strategy, considering the collapsing popularity of sedans.
Last year, Audi sold only 1,406 A8s in the United States, which was 13.6% down from 2024. In the meantime, BMW moved 11,393 7 Series examples (including the i7), and Mercedes-Benz delivered 7,408 units last year.
Photo: Audi Considering the circumstances, Audi might resort to the MSB architecture, which underpins the Porsche Panamera . The MSB is developed for front-engine, rear- or all-wheel-drive luxury vehicles and is capable of supporting both combustion and hybrid powertrains.
It is a race against time for Audi to find a way for the A8 to go into production before the end of the decade. With the final D5 generation model rolling off the assembly line in October and the next-gen sedan not arriving until late in the decade, Audi will have a multi-year gap without a flagship sedan in its portfolio.
During this interval, the upcoming three-row Audi Q9 SUV will serve as the brand's flagship model, sitting at the top of the lineup. The Q9 will be built in Perry, Georgia, at the Middle Georgia Mega Site near Macon. Last month, Audi announced plans for a $4 billion investment and a second-phase $3 million expansion of its first-ever manufacturing center in the United States.
